You will serve as a Technical Project Lead (TPL) for the Afloat Counter Unmanned Systems (ACUS) portfolio.
You will be responsible for the technical baseline and risk management, employing an agile, iterative approach to evaluate emerging technologies and ensure the continuous delivery of safe, authorized, and effective C-UxS solutions.
You will lead technical efforts by coordinating activities across Ship Integration and Certification, Launcher and Gun-Based Effectors, Fire Direction, and Systems Engineering.
You will provide hands-on guidance to a diverse engineering team, ensuring strict adherence to engineering best practices and driving the technical review of all deliverables.
You will lead a cross-functional team to ensure successful project execution and alignment with program and sponsor goals, while fostering collaboration across technical and programmatic disciplines to achieve project success.
You will evaluate emerging technologies and systems to accelerate delivery of rapid capabilities to the Fleet, employing a highly agile, iterative engineering approach focused on continuous/rapid deployment of effective ship self-defense solutions.
You will provide hands-on technical leadership to a diverse engineering team, resolving complex system issues, enforcing engineering best practices, and validating all technical deliverables prior to fleet release.
You will serve as the primary technical engineering authority, owning the engineering approach, driving key design decisions, and actively managing technical risks to ensure system viability.
You will formulate strategic technical guidance and roadmaps in collaboration with the ACUS leadership team to ensure project activities integrate seamlessly into the overall program strategy and support the long-term viability of C-UxS capabilities.
You will lead the technical execution and delivery of project products to the Fleet, interfacing directly with program offices, In­Service Engineering Agents (ISEA), and stakeholders to ensure seamless integration.
You will manage, execute, and report on project operations, serving as the first line of escalation for project-specific successes and challenges, and collaborating closely with program leadership to address and resolve issues.
You will execute rigorous administrative project management duties, including developing Statements of Work (SOW), spend plans, and ensuring compliance with NSWCDD, E Department, Division, and Afloat Counter Unmanned Systems (ACUS) policies.
You will serve as the primary project representative, communicating effectively with team members, sponsors, and external organizations (as delegated by the PM) to ensure complete transparency and alignment with overarching program goals.
Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the ND-04 (GS-12/13 equivalent) pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector as a professional engineer or scientist leading the technical architecture, design, and systems engineering of Department of War weapon systems.

Examples of qualifying experience may include: (1) Serving as a technical authority or lead systems engineer, owning the technical approach and making key engineering design decisions for complex weapon systems, effectors, or fire direction systems; (2) Providing hands-on technical leadership to engineering teams, including the review and validation of technical deliverables, the execution of formal systems engineering processes, and the active management of technical risks; (3) Leading technical efforts in design, development and integration of emerging capabilities.

Förderprojekt für junge Frauen mit Fluchthintergrund | Kanton Zürich
Die impulsarbeit gmbh entwickelt in Winterthur ein neues Förderprogramm für junge Frauen mit Fluchthintergrund.
Ziel ist die persönliche, gesellschaftliche und wirtschaftliche Emanzipation der Teilnehmerinnen. Die Frauen sollen ihre Ressourcen und Handlungsmöglichkeiten erweitern und schrittweise die Voraussetzungen schaffen, ihr Leben selbstbestimmt und möglichst unabhängig von staatlicher Unterstützung gestalten zu können.
Für den Aufbau und die fachliche Entwicklung des Programms suchen wir per 1. Oktober 2026 eine Projektleiterin (40 %). Die Stelle ist zunächst auf ein Jahr befristet.
Ein Programm mit Zeit für Entwicklung
Für die Aufbau- und Entwicklungsphase stehen substanzielle private Mittel zur Verfügung. Dadurch kann das Programm ohne kurzfristigen Finanzierungs-, Vermittlungs- oder Mengendruck entwickelt werden.
Unterschiedliche Ansätze können sorgfältig erprobt, ausgewertet und weiterentwickelt werden. Eine externe Wirkungsmessung begleitet das Programm und stellt sicher, dass Erkenntnisse systematisch in die kontinuierliche Qualitätsentwicklung einfliessen.
Ziel ist ein fachlich fundiertes, lernendes und langfristig anschlussfähiges Fördermodell. Die Zusammenarbeit mit Gemeinden, Kanton, Fachstellen und bestehenden Integrationsstrukturen ist ausdrücklich erwünscht.
Zwei Arbeitstage – zwei unterschiedliche Erfahrungsräume
Die 40%-Stelle verteilt sich grundsätzlich auf zwei Arbeitstage pro Woche.
1. Tag: Förderung, Arbeitsintegration und Fallarbeit
Die Teilnehmerinnen arbeiten in einem realen betrieblichen Umfeld und sammeln konkrete Arbeitserfahrungen. Die Projektleiterin begleitet diesen Prozess fachlich und individuell.

· arbeitsintegrative Begleitung

· individuelle Förderplanung

· Fallarbeit

· Erkennen und Aktivieren vorhandener Ressourcen

· Reflexion der Erfahrungen im Betrieb

· Entwicklung beruflicher und persönlicher Perspektiven

· Zusammenarbeit mit Betrieben, Fachstellen und weiteren Beteiligten

· Planung geeigneter nächster Entwicklungsschritte
2. Tag: Waldtag und individuelles Coaching
Der zweite Tag schafft bewusst einen anderen Rahmen. Ein Teil des Tages findet gemeinsam im Wald statt. Natur, Bewegung, gemeinsames Tun und Gespräche eröffnen andere Zugänge zu Ressourcen, Beziehungen und persönlichen Themen.
Ergänzend finden individuelle Coachings statt. Hier können persönliche Ziele, aktuelle Herausforderungen, Ressourcen und nächste Schritte vertieft bearbeitet werden.
Beide Tage gehören zusammen: konkrete Erfahrung und Arbeitsintegration auf der einen Seite, Reflexion, individuelle Entwicklung und Stabilisierung auf der anderen.
Fachlicher Hintergrund
Wir suchen eine Frau mit einem Abschluss in Sozialer Arbeit FH oder einem fundierten fachlichen Hintergrund in kunstbasierten, kunstpädagogischen oder kunsttherapeutischen Methoden.

s.h: Von Vorteil sind Kenntnisse und praktische Erfahrungen mit
s.t:
· Empowerment und Ressourcenaktivierung

· lösungsorientierter Beratung

· partizipativen Ansätzen

· Lebensweltorientierung

· Capability- und Befähigungsansätzen

· traumasensibler Arbeit

· kreativen und kunstbasierten Methoden
Erfahrung in der Projekt- und Aufbauarbeit ist von grossem Vorteil.
Von sehr grossem Vorteil sind Erfahrungen mit Förder- und Integrationsangeboten sowie in der direkten Arbeit mit Frauen mit Fluchthintergrund.
Gesucht wird eine eigenständige, reflektierte und entwicklungsorientierte Persönlichkeit, die fachliche Qualität mit Freude an Aufbauarbeit verbindet.
Frauenspezifisches Setting
Die Tätigkeit umfasst die unmittelbare Arbeit mit teilweise vulnerablen Frauen mit Fluchterfahrung innerhalb eines geschützten, frauenspezifischen Vertrauenssettings. Die Ausschreibung richtet sich deshalb an Frauen. Diese Anforderung ergibt sich aus der konkreten Funktion und dem Schutzkonzept des Programms.

II. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES Under the general direction of the Principal Inspector (Maintenance or Avionics) or Supervisory Principal Inspector (Maintenance or Avionics) accomplishes the following duties: A.

Technical Administration On a continuing basis, ensures assigned organizations are properly and adequately organized, staffed and equipped; establishes and conducts adequate training programs; maintains record keeping systems; and facilities and ensures procedures meet all regulatory requirements.

Chairs joint Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and industry meetings. Maintains regular contact with organizations assigned and coordinates with top management officials. Requires or directs correction of any deficiencies/discrepancies and refuses or withdraws approval if they cannot be resolved.

Develops avionics program requirements through participation on maintenance review boards. Coordinates minimum equipment list (MEL) approvals with the principal operations inspector. Takes enforcement action in instances of noncompliance with the MEL.

Responsible for conducting enforcement investigations and preparation of final reports and recommendations on disposition. Performs or supervises the emergency suspension of certificates or cancellation of operations specifications. Conducts or directs the reexamination of certificated airmen or recertification of an operator or agency.

Conducts investigations of public complaints, congressional inquiries, and aircraft incidents and accidents. Provides verbal and/or written technical assistance to legal counsel, testifies at court trials and formal hearings, and gives dispositions.

Coordinates with geographic inspectors for the accomplishment of non-routine air carrier surveillance. B. Certification Responsible for initial and ongoing certification of air carriers, aircraft, airmen, and air agencies. Makes recommendations on the appointment of designees.

Evaluates requests to operate under conditions not previously specified in the airworthiness portion of the operations specifications and approves/disapproves requests providing additional conditions and limitations as needed. Provides guidance to the assigned air carrier in the development of required maintenance manuals and record keeping systems.

Reviews and determines adequacy of manuals associated with the air carrier¿s airworthiness programs and revisions. Ensures manuals and revisions comply with regulatory requirements, prescribe safe practices, and furnish clear and specific instructions governing airworthiness programs. Approves operations specifications and amendments.

Determines if the maintenance facilities being established or contract arrangements entered into by air carrier for the purpose of overhaul work, major repairs, alterations, and other maintenance are satisfactory. Reviews changes and negotiates with air carrier management to resolve problems.

Determines if overhaul and inspection time limitations warrant revision. Evaluates an operator¿s proposed reliability programs for compliance with national policies. Advises operator of deficiencies and required changes. Approves/disapproves reliability programs.

Determines if the air carrier¿s training program meets the requirements of 14 CFR, is compatible with the airworthiness program, is properly organized and effectively conducted, and results in trained and competent personnel. Directs or participates in flight evaluations to determine compliance with 14 CFR.

Recommends changes that will be required prior to approval. C. Surveillance Under guidance of the Principal Inspector, directs the inspection and surveillance of the air carrier¿s continuous airworthiness program in regard to assigned aircraft fleet assignment(s).

Monitors all phases of the air carrier¿s airworthiness operation, including the maintenance, engineering, quality control, production control, training, and reliability programs.
Applicants must meet the Office of Personnel Management Qualification Standards: General Requirements for All Positions: Not more than two separate incidents involving Federal Aviation regulations violations in the last 5 years Valid State driver's license Fluency in the English language No chemical dependencies or drug abuse that could interfere with job performance, and High School diploma or equivalent.

Medical Requirements: Applicants must be physically able to perform the duties of the Aviation Safety Inspector position in a safe and efficient manner, and must meet all of the following requirements: Have good distant vision in each eye and be able to read, without strain, printed materials the size of typewritten characters (glasses and contact lenses permitted); Have the ability to hear the conversational voice (hearing aid permitted); and Not have any physical condition that would cause them to be a hazard to themselves or others that would interfere with their ability to fly as passengers in a variety of aircraft.

In addition, applicants for positions that require participation in the operation of the aircraft must: Possess a valid second ¿ class medical certificate in accordance with FAA regulations; and Pass recurrent medical examinations as prescribed by the FAA.

Applicants not requiring valid second-class medical certificates who are tentatively selected will be required to: Provide documentation from a board-certified physician certifying that they meet the minimal medical requirements; or Individuals who do not meet the minimum medical requirements but who are otherwise qualified will receive an individualized assessment to determine whether they can perform the essential functions of the position.

When the predominant work involves air carrier avionics, applicants for Aviation Safety Inspector (Airworthiness) positions must meet all of the following requirements. Aircraft avionics experience involving the maintenance, repair, and troubleshooting of installed avionics systems on aircraft.

Avionics maintenance experience on aircraft of more than 12,500 pounds maximum certificated takeoff weight. Aircraft avionics work experience (which could include supervision or auditing) in a repair station; air carrier repair facility; military repair facility; or local, state, or Federal governmental agency within the last 3 years.

* **Leadership basé sur la confiance :** Vous dirigez et soutenez votre équipe (4 collaborateurs) et faites avancer activement la numérisation des processus internes.
* **Innovation & développement :** Vous êtes responsable de la conception, du développement et de la mise en œuvre de nouvelles fonctionnalités et processus dans le paysage SAP (MM/HCM) et le système de gestion du temps.
* **Responsabilité système & processus ainsi que gestion de projet :** Vous entretenez, supervisez et développez continuellement les modules SAP MM et HCM ainsi que notre système d-enregistrement du temps et des frais "Time". Vous êtes également responsable de la gestion des autorisations. Vous dirigez ou accompagnez des projets (partiels) importants et représentez votre département dans des comités internes et externes.
* **Compétence d-interface (SPOC) :** Vous êtes le point central pour SAP au sein de la police cantonale et maintenez un contact étroit avec le CCOE SAP de l-administration financière ainsi qu-avec le helpdesk interne.
* **Transmission des connaissances & support :** Vous êtes responsable du support aux utilisateurs clés, documentez les nouveautés (Solman, EnableNow, Viflow, Aviso) et animez des formations pour cadres en allemand et en français.
Votre profil
* **Base solide :** Un diplôme supérieur achevé (FH, université) en informatique de gestion, économie d-entreprise ou une qualification comparable, combiné à une expérience IT approfondie et un savoir-faire dans le domaine financier.
* **Expertise SAP :** Plusieurs années d-expérience approfondie avec les modules SAP MM et HCM.
* **Expérience en gestion de projet & leadership :** Vous avez déjà dirigé des projets avec succès et possédez de l-expérience dans la conduite, la motivation et le développement d-équipes.
* **Mode de pensée :** Fortes capacités analytiques, pensée systémique, orientation solution ainsi qu-une affinité marquée pour les domaines techniques.
* **Personnalité & langue :** Vous êtes une personne motivée et socialement compétente, qui communique de manière adaptée à tous les niveaux hiérarchiques. Comme vous formez également le cadre francophone, vous vous exprimez couramment à l-oral en français.
Nous vous offrons
* Prestations sociales et prévoyance attractives
* Employeur sûr et système salarial transparent, cadeaux d-ancienneté (temps ou argent)
* Environnement dynamique dans une grande entreprise, contacts passionnants avec des personnes du quotidien policier
* Valeurs fondées, formes de respect mutuel
* Développement du personnel adapté au niveau : intégration compétente, soutien à la formation individuelle, développement de la part des femmes
* Modèles de travail flexibles : temps de travail annuel, modèles à temps partiel, télétravail
* Promotion de la santé : diverses offres sportives et culturelles, bilan de santé

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster.

Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities.

A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

The International Rescue Committee helps people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their future.

Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC works with people forced to flee from war, conflict and disaster and the host communities that support them, as well as with those who remain within their homes and communities.

At work today in over 40 countries and 22 U.S. cities, we restore safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure.
The IT department provides end-to-end solutions for the organization including application development & integration, system deployment, user experience and change management, quality assurance & testing, and overall Project Management in an effort to help the organization determine and implement the best solutions for its business needs.

This is a rare opportunity to sit at the center of one of the most consequential applications of AI in the social sector. As the IRC's AI Program Manager, you will help shape how a global humanitarian organization — operating in over 40 countries — harnesses artificial intelligence to improve outcomes for some of the world's most vulnerable people. This is not a role managing technology for its own sake; it is a role where smart, responsible AI adoption can directly accelerate impact at scale.
You will lead and coordinate the IRC's most important AI initiatives: driving enterprise AI projects from concept to delivery, ensuring that AI tools adopted across the organization are evaluated rigorously and responsibly, and coordinating the cross-functional teams working to embed AI into how the IRC operates. You will work at the intersection of technology, program delivery, and organizational change — partnering with senior leaders, technical experts, and frontline staff across the globe.
The right candidate is a fast-moving, proactive problem-solver who thrives in ambiguity, brings structure to complex and evolving landscapes, and is energized by the challenge of building something new in an environment where the stakes are high and the work is genuinely meaningful.
This role reports to the AI Governance and Transformation Lead, and works in close partnership with Director, IT Project and Portfolio Management, AI project leads, senior sponsors, and a broad community of practice across the organization.

AI Governance (60%)
The IRC is committed to adopting AI responsibly. As part of this, the organization has established a structured review process for AI use cases that carry potential high risks — whether related to data privacy, security, bias, or ethical considerations. As coordinator of this process, you will:
Manage the intake and documentation of AI use cases and tools flagged for high-risk review.
Assign cases to appropriate domain reviewers (e.g., legal, security, data protection, ethics) and coordinate their timely completion.
Maintain templates, trackers, and a full audit trail of all reviewed use cases and decisions.
Communicate clearly with requestors on process, status, and outcomes.
Draft and maintain guidance documentation, publishing decisions and resources to the IRC's internal staff portal.
Prepare agendas, materials, and logistics for review panel meetings.
Support the implementation of IRC’s enterprise AI policy, building out the necessary tools and processes in close collaboration with others.
Enterprise AI Project Management (40%)
Lead project management for high-priority, organization-wide AI initiatives. Responsibilities include:
Developing and maintaining detailed project plans, work breakdown structures, risk registers, and terms of reference.
Facilitating scrum, sprint planning, and retrospective meetings; driving delivery against milestones.
Designing and executing testing, rollout, and change management plans in partnership with cross-functional stakeholders.
Producing regular status reports for senior leadership, clearly communicating scope, progress, risks, and decisions.
Proactively surfacing and resolving blockers, issues, and risks before they become critical.

Maintains a productive working relationship with other project managers, business owners, AI project leads, senior sponsors of AI strategy initiatives, legal, security, and data protection teams, system users, and vendors.

Dank Ihres Wissens, Ihrer Kreativität und Ihren Erfahrungen begleiten Sie Kundenprojekte von der Konzept\- über die Design\- und Prototypenphase bis zur Produktverifikation.
